1	# Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities
2	
3	## Source
4	https://climate.nasa.gov/vital-signs/carbon-dioxide/ and Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Global Carbon Budget 2025)
5	
6	## Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration
7	
8	The latest measurement from NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory (February 2026) records atmospheric CO₂ at **429 parts per million (ppm)**. This represents a more than 50% increase from the pre-industrial baseline of approximately 280 ppm. The current level is at least 1.5 times greater than the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a change that took thousands of years then but has occurred in roughly two centuries now. Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm the sharp acceleration, linked primarily to the burning of coal, oil, and natural gas.
9	
10	## Global Emissions Trajectory (1750–2024)
11	
12	Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible. Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century. In **1950**, the world emitted roughly **6 billion tonnes** of CO₂. By **1990**, emissions had nearly quadrupled to over **20 billion tonnes**. Today, global annual emissions from fossil fuels and industry exceed **35 billion tonnes**. While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked.
13	
14	![Annual CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
15	
16	## Who Emits the Most? Country-Level Totals
17	
18	China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin, producing over 12 billion tonnes annually — more than one-quarter of the global total. The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes. India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes. Europe's share has fallen substantially.
19	
20	| Country / Region | Approx. Annual CO₂ (billion t) | Share of Global | Trend (recent) |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| China | ~12.5 | ~27% | Slight increase |
23	| United States | ~5.0 | ~14% | Declining |
24	| India | ~3.0 | ~8% | Rising |
25	| EU-27 | ~2.7 | ~7% | Declining |
26	| Germany | ~0.6 | ~1.7% | Declining |
27	| United Kingdom | ~0.3 | ~0.9% | Declining |
28	| Brazil | ~0.5 | ~1.4% | Roughly stable |
29	| France | ~0.3 | ~0.8% | Declining |
30	
31	In 1900, Europe and the US accounted for more than 90% of global emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third, while Asia — home to nearly 60% of the world's population — produces roughly half of all emissions. Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%, comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.
32	
33	## Per Capita Emissions: Extreme Inequalities
34	
35	Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's highest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the US, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.
36	
37	![Per capita CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
38	
39	| Country | Per Capita CO₂ (tonnes/year) |
40	|---|---|
41	| United States | ~15 |
42	| Canada | ~13 |
43	| Australia | ~15 |
44	| South Africa | ~8 |
45	| China | ~9 |
46	| EU-27 | ~7 |
47	| World average | ~5 |
48	| United Kingdom | ~4 |
49	| France | ~4 |
50	| India | ~2 |
51	| Kenya | <1 |
52	| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 |
53	
54	The gap between the highest and lowest per capita emitters is approximately **150-fold**: the average American or Australian emits in under two days what the average person in Chad or Niger emits in an entire year. Importantly, countries with similar living standards can differ significantly — France and the UK have much lower per capita emissions than Germany or the Netherlands, largely because of their energy mix (higher nuclear and renewable shares).
55	
56	## 2024 Annual Change in Emissions
57

## Source
https://climate.nasa.gov/vital-signs/carbon-dioxide/ and Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Global Carbon Budget 2025)

## Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration

The latest measurement from NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory (February 2026) records atmospheric CO₂ at **429 parts per million (ppm)**. This represents a more than 50% increase from the pre-industrial baseline of approximately 280 ppm. The current level is at least 1.5 times greater than the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a change that took thousands of years then but has occurred in roughly two centuries now. Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm the sharp acceleration, linked primarily to the burning of coal, oil, and natural gas.

## Global Emissions Trajectory (1750–2024)

Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible. Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century. In **1950**, the world emitted roughly **6 billion tonnes** of CO₂. By **1990**, emissions had nearly quadrupled to over **20 billion tonnes**. Today, global annual emissions from fossil fuels and industry exceed **35 billion tonnes**. While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked.

![Annual CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_3.jpg)

## Who Emits the Most? Country-Level Totals

China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin, producing over 12 billion tonnes annually — more than one-quarter of the global total. The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes. India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes. Europe's share has fallen substantially.

| Country / Region | Approx. Annual CO₂ (billion t) | Share of Global | Trend (recent) |
|---|---|---|---|
| China | ~12.5 | ~27% | Slight increase |
| United States | ~5.0 | ~14% | Declining |
| India | ~3.0 | ~8% | Rising |
| EU-27 | ~2.7 | ~7% | Declining |
| Germany | ~0.6 | ~1.7% | Declining |
| United Kingdom | ~0.3 | ~0.9% | Declining |
| Brazil | ~0.5 | ~1.4% | Roughly stable |
| France | ~0.3 | ~0.8% | Declining |

In 1900, Europe and the US accounted for more than 90% of global emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third, while Asia — home to nearly 60% of the world's population — produces roughly half of all emissions. Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%, comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.

## Per Capita Emissions: Extreme Inequalities

Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's highest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the US, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.

|---|---|

| EU-27 | ~7 |
| World average | ~5 |
| United Kingdom | ~4 |
| France | ~4 |
| India | ~2 |
| Kenya | <1 |
| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 |

- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.

### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content

- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.

### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders

- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.

### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language

- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.

### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately

- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.

### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe

- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.

## Common Traps

- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.

def add_bg(slide, color):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=DARK_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.2):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    p.space_after = Pt(0)
    if line_spacing != 1.2:
        p.line_spacing = Pt(font_size * line_spacing)
    return txBox

def add_multi_text(slide, left, top, width, height, lines, font_size=16,
                   color=DARK_TEXT, font_name="Calibri", bullet=False,
                   line_spacing=1.5, bold_list=None):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if i == 0:

        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(int(font_size * 0.5))
        if bold_list and i < len(bold_list):

    return txBox

    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg_color
    shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xDD)
    shape.line.width = Pt(1)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.2),
                width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.7), number,
                font_size=28, bold=True, color=num_color, alignment=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.9),
                width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.6), label,

OUT = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# Colors
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x2A, 0x4A)
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x00, 0x7B, 0xBB)
ACCENT_TEAL = RGBColor(0x00, 0xA6, 0x9C)
LIGHT_BG = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xF7, 0xFA)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
DARK_TEXT = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x2A, 0x4A)
GRAY_TEXT = RGBColor(0x5A, 0x6A, 0x7A)
RED_ACCENT = RGBColor(0xE0, 0x4F, 0x4F)
GREEN_ACCENT = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x8B, 0x57)
ORANGE_ACCENT = RGBColor(0xE8, 0x8D, 0x2A)
BAR_COLORS = [
    RGBColor(0xC0, 0x39, 0x2B),  # US - red
    RGBColor(0xE8, 0x6D, 0x2A),  # Canada - orange
    RGBColor(0xE8, 0xB8, 0x2A),  # China - gold
    RGBColor(0x2E, 0x86, 0xAB),  # EU-27 - blue
    RGBColor(0x5A, 0x6A, 0x7A),  # World avg - gray
    RGBColor(0x00, 0x7B, 0xBB),  # UK - accent blue
    RGBColor(0x2E, 0x8B, 0x57),  # India - green
    RGBColor(0x8B, 0x6F, 0x4E),  # Chad/Kenya - brown
]

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

SW = prs.slide_width
SH = prs.slide_height

def add_blank_slide():
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    return prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

def add_bg(slide, color):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=DARK_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.2):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    p.space_after = Pt(0)
    if line_spacing != 1.2:
        p.line_spacing = Pt(font_size * line_spacing)
    return txBox

def add_multi_text(slide, left, top, width, height, lines, font_size=16,
                   color=DARK_TEXT, font_name="Calibri", bullet=False,
                   line_spacing=1.5, bold_list=None):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = ("  \u2022  " + line) if bullet else line
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(int(font_size * 0.5))
        if bold_list and i < len(bold_list):
            p.font.bold = bold_list[i]
    return txBox

def add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, width, height, color=ACCENT_BLUE):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def add_stat_card(slide, left, top, width, height, number, label,
                  num_color=ACCENT_BLUE, bg_color=WHITE):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg_color
    shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xDD)
    shape.line.width = Pt(1)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.2),
                width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.7), number,
                font_size=28, bold=True, color=num_color, alignment=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.9),
                width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.6), label,
                font_size=12, color=GRAY_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

def add_image_safe(slide, path, left, top, width=None, height=None):
    if os.path.exists(path):
        kwargs = {"image_file": path, "left": left, "top": top}
        if width: kwargs["width"] = width
        if height: kwargs["height"] = height
        slide.shapes.add_picture(**kwargs)
        return True
    return False

def slide_title_bar(slide, title, subtitle=None):
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SW, Inches(1.1), DARK_BG)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.15), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
                title, font_size=24, bold=True, color=WHITE, font_name="Calibri")
    if subtitle:
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.7), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.35),
                    subtitle, font_size=13, color=RGBColor(0xBB, 0xCC, 0xDD), font_name="Calibri")

# ── SLIDE 1: Title ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, DARK_BG)
add_accent_bar(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(0.08), Inches(2.0), ACCENT_TEAL)
add_textbox(s, Inches(1.2), Inches(2.0), Inches(10), Inches(1.2),
            "Global CO\u2082 Emissions", font_size=44, bold=True, color=WHITE)
add_textbox(s, Inches(1.2), Inches(3.1), Inches(10), Inches(0.9),
            "Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities",
            font_size=28, color=RGBColor(0x7E, 0xC8, 0xE3))
add_textbox(s, Inches(1.2), Inches(4.3), Inches(10), Inches(0.5),
            "1750 \u2013 2024  |  Data from Global Carbon Budget 2025 & NASA",
            font_size=16, color=RGBColor(0x99, 0xAA, 0xBB))
add_textbox(s, Inches(1.2), Inches(5.3), Inches(10), Inches(0.4),
            "For policy analysts and climate negotiators",
            font_size=14, color=RGBColor(0x77, 0x88, 0x99))

# ── SLIDE 2: Atmospheric CO₂ Milestone ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "Atmospheric CO\u2082 Reaches 429 ppm \u2014 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels")

add_stat_card(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5), Inches(1.7),
              "429 ppm", "Mauna Loa, February 2026", num_color=RED_ACCENT)
add_stat_card(s, Inches(4.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5), Inches(1.7),
              "~280 ppm", "Pre-industrial baseline", num_color=ACCENT_BLUE)
add_stat_card(s, Inches(8.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(3.5), Inches(1.7),
              ">50%", "Increase since pre-industrial era", num_color=ORANGE_ACCENT)

add_multi_text(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.7), Inches(11.5), Inches(3.0), [
    "Current CO\u2082 is at least 1.5\u00d7 greater than the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago.",
    "That ice-age change took thousands of years \u2014 the current rise has occurred in roughly two centuries.",
    "The acceleration is linked primarily to burning coal, oil, and natural gas, confirmed by ground-based and satellite measurements.",
], font_size=16, bullet=True, color=DARK_TEXT, line_spacing=1.4)

# ── SLIDE 3: Global Emissions Trajectory ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "Global Fossil Fuel CO\u2082 Emissions Grew Six-Fold: 6 Bt to 35+ Bt")

# Left side: key stats
add_stat_card(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(2.8), Inches(1.4),
              "~6 Bt", "1950 annual emissions", num_color=ACCENT_BLUE)
add_stat_card(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.2), Inches(2.8), Inches(1.4),
              "~20 Bt", "1990 annual emissions", num_color=ORANGE_ACCENT)
add_stat_card(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.9), Inches(2.8), Inches(1.4),
              ">35 Bt", "2024 annual emissions", num_color=RED_ACCENT)

add_multi_text(s, Inches(4.2), Inches(1.5), Inches(8.5), Inches(2.5), [
    "Before the Industrial Revolution, CO\u2082 emissions were negligible.",
    "Growth remained slow until the mid-20th century, then accelerated sharply.",
    "Emissions nearly quadrupled from 1950 to 1990, then almost doubled again by 2024.",
    "While growth rates have slowed in recent years, global emissions have not yet peaked.",
], font_size=15, bullet=True, color=DARK_TEXT)

# Note about figure
add_textbox(s, Inches(4.2), Inches(4.5), Inches(8.5), Inches(0.4),
            "See figure_3.jpg for the annual CO\u2082 emissions by country time series.",
            font_size=12, color=GRAY_TEXT)

# ── SLIDE 4: China Surpasses US ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "China Now Emits Over 12 Billion Tonnes \u2014 More Than Double the United States")

# Data table
countries = [
    ("China", "~12.5 Bt", "~27%", "Slight increase"),
    ("United States", "~5.0 Bt", "~14%", "Declining"),
    ("India", "~3.0 Bt", "~8%", "Rising"),
    ("EU-27", "~2.7 Bt", "~7%", "Declining"),
    ("Germany", "~0.6 Bt", "~1.7%", "Declining"),
    ("United Kingdom", "~0.3 Bt", "~0.9%", "Declining"),
    ("Brazil", "~0.5 Bt", "~1.4%", "Stable"),
    ("France", "~0.3 Bt", "~0.8%", "Declining"),
]

tbl_left = Inches(0.8)
tbl_top = Inches(1.5)
cols_w = [Inches(2.5), Inches(2.2), Inches(2.0), Inches(2.2)]
row_h = Inches(0.45)
headers = ["Country / Region", "Annual CO\u2082", "Global Share", "Recent Trend"]

table_shape = s.shapes.add_table(len(countries) + 1, 4,
                                  tbl_left, tbl_top,
                                  sum(c for c in cols_w), row_h * (len(countries) + 1))
table = table_shape.table
for i, w in enumerate(cols_w):
    table.columns[i].width = w

for ci, h in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0, ci)
    cell.text = h
    for p in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
        p.font.size = Pt(13)
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG

for ri, row_data in enumerate(countries):
    for ci, val in enumerate(row_data):
        cell = table.cell(ri + 1, ci)
        cell.text = val
        for p in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
            p.font.size = Pt(12)
            p.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
            p.font.name = "Calibri"
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = WHITE if ri % 2 == 0 else RGBColor(0xEB, 0xEF, 0xF5)

# Add figure_3
add_image_safe(s, f"{ASSETS}/figure_3.jpg", Inches(9.3), Inches(1.5),
               width=Inches(3.7), height=Inches(5.0))

# ── SLIDE 5: Regional Share Shift ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "Asia Now Accounts for ~50% of Global Emissions; US + Europe Below One-Third")

# 1900 vs 2024 comparison blocks
def add_share_block(slide, left, top, year, items, accent):
    add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, Inches(5.0), Inches(0.55), accent)
    add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.07), Inches(4.5), Inches(0.45),
                year, font_size=22, bold=True, color=WHITE)
    for i, (region, share, bar_w_pct) in enumerate(items):
        y = top + Inches(0.7) + Inches(i * 0.75)
        add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.1), y, Inches(2.2), Inches(0.35),
                    region, font_size=14, bold=True, color=DARK_TEXT)
        add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(0.1), y + Inches(0.3), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.3),
                    share, font_size=13, color=GRAY_TEXT)
        bar_w = Inches(2.8 * bar_w_pct)
        bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
                                      left + Inches(2.2), y + Inches(0.05),
                                      bar_w, Inches(0.3))
        bar.fill.solid()
        bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = accent
        bar.line.fill.background()

items_1900 = [
    ("Europe + US", ">90%", 0.92),
    ("Asia", "<5%", 0.05),
    ("Rest of World", "~5%", 0.05),
]
items_2024 = [
    ("Asia", "~50%", 0.50),
    ("Europe + US", "<33%", 0.32),
    ("Africa & S. America", "~3\u20134% each", 0.07),
]

add_share_block(s, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.4), "1900", items_1900, RGBColor(0x7B, 0x8D, 0xA3))
add_share_block(s, Inches(6.6), Inches(1.4), "2024", items_2024, ACCENT_TEAL)

add_textbox(s, Inches(0.6), Inches(5.5), Inches(12.0), Inches(1.0),
            "Africa and South America each contribute only 3\u20134% of global emissions \u2014 comparable to international aviation and shipping combined. "
            "In 1950, Europe and the US still represented over 85% of global emissions.",
            font_size=14, color=GRAY_TEXT)

# ── SLIDE 6: Per Capita 150× Gap ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "Per Capita Gap: 15 t in the US vs. 0.1 t in Chad \u2014 a 150\u00d7 Disparity")

pc_data = [
    ("United States", 15.0),
    ("Canada", 13.0),
    ("China", 9.0),
    ("EU-27", 7.0),
    ("World average", 5.0),
    ("United Kingdom", 4.0),
    ("India", 2.0),
    ("Chad / Kenya", 0.1),
]

bar_area_left = Inches(0.6)
bar_area_top = Inches(1.4)
max_val = 16.0
max_bar_w = Inches(6.5)
bar_h = Inches(0.5)
bar_gap = Inches(0.22)

for i, (country, val) in enumerate(pc_data):
    y = bar_area_top + (bar_h + bar_gap) * i
    add_textbox(s, bar_area_left, y, Inches(2.0), bar_h,
                country, font_size=13, bold=True, color=DARK_TEXT,
                alignment=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    bw = int(max_bar_w * (val / max_val))
    if bw < Inches(0.15):
        bw = Inches(0.15)
    bar = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
                              bar_area_left + Inches(2.15), y + Inches(0.05),
                              bw, Inches(0.38))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = BAR_COLORS[i]
    bar.line.fill.background()
    label = f"~{val} t" if val >= 1 else f"~{val} t"
    add_textbox(s, bar_area_left + Inches(2.15) + bw + Inches(0.1), y,
                Inches(1.0), bar_h, label, font_size=12, color=GRAY_TEXT)

# figure_1 reference
add_image_safe(s, f"{ASSETS}/figure_1.jpg", Inches(9.3), Inches(1.4),
               width=Inches(3.7), height=Inches(4.5))

add_textbox(s, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.6), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.5),
            "The average American emits in under two days what the average person in Chad emits in an entire year.",
            font_size=13, bold=True, color=RED_ACCENT)

# ── SLIDE 7: 2024 Annual Change Map ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "2024 Snapshot: US and Europe Cut Emissions While Russia and SE Asia Increase")

# Left: commentary
add_multi_text(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(5.0), [
    "United States and much of Europe: declines of \u22121% to \u22125% (shown in blue on the map).",
    "Russia, parts of Southeast Asia, and several African nations: increases of +2% to +10% (orange/red).",
    "Some South American countries experienced very large percentage increases (>10%).",
    "The mixed picture shows that while some major economies are decarbonizing, global emissions have not yet peaked.",
], font_size=15, bullet=True, color=DARK_TEXT, line_spacing=1.5)

# figure_4
add_image_safe(s, f"{ASSETS}/figure_4.jpg", Inches(6.8), Inches(1.4),
               width=Inches(6.0), height=Inches(5.2))

# ── SLIDE 8: Energy Mix Drives Differences ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, LIGHT_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "Energy Mix Explains Why France Emits Far Less Per Capita Than Germany")

add_multi_text(s, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(1.5), [
    "Countries with similar living standards can have very different per capita emissions depending on their energy sources.",
    "Nuclear and renewable energy dramatically reduce per capita CO\u2082, even at high levels of prosperity.",
], font_size=16, bullet=True, color=DARK_TEXT)

# Comparison table
tbl_left2 = Inches(1.5)
tbl_top2 = Inches(3.2)
cols2 = [Inches(2.8), Inches(3.5), Inches(2.5)]
row_h2 = Inches(0.6)
headers2 = ["Country", "Key Energy Sources", "Per Capita CO\u2082"]
tbl_data2 = [
    ("France", "High nuclear (~70%), growing renewables", "~4 t/year"),
    ("United Kingdom", "Nuclear + offshore wind, declining coal", "~4 t/year"),
    ("Germany", "Higher fossil fuel share, coal phase-out ongoing", "~8 t/year*"),
    ("Netherlands", "Natural gas dependent, offshore wind growing", "~8 t/year*"),
]

table_shape2 = s.shapes.add_table(len(tbl_data2) + 1, 3,
                                   tbl_left2, tbl_top2,
                                   sum(c for c in cols2), row_h2 * (len(tbl_data2) + 1))
table2 = table_shape2.table
for i, w in enumerate(cols2):
    table2.columns[i].width = w

for ci, h in enumerate(headers2):
    cell = table2.cell(0, ci)
    cell.text = h
    for p in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
        p.font.size = Pt(14)
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG

for ri, row_data in enumerate(tbl_data2):
    for ci, val in enumerate(row_data):
        cell = table2.cell(ri + 1, ci)
        cell.text = val
        for p in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
            p.font.size = Pt(13)
            p.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
            p.font.name = "Calibri"
        bg = RGBColor(0xE0, 0xF5, 0xF0) if ri < 2 else RGBColor(0xFD, 0xEC, 0xE0)
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg

add_textbox(s, Inches(1.5), Inches(6.3), Inches(10), Inches(0.4),
            "* Approximate; Germany\u2019s per capita figure reflects its overall energy mix including coal and industrial base.",
            font_size=11, color=GRAY_TEXT)

# ── SLIDE 9: Key Takeaways ──
s = add_blank_slide()
add_bg(s, DARK_BG)
slide_title_bar(s, "Key Takeaways: Emissions Are Still Rising, But the Map of Responsibility Is Shifting")
# Override title bar to match dark bg
add_accent_bar(s, Inches(0), Inches(0), SW, Inches(1.1), ACCENT_TEAL)
add_textbox(s, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.15), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.7),
            "Key Takeaways", font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE)

takeaways = [
    "Global CO\u2082 emissions now exceed 35 billion tonnes per year and have not yet peaked, despite slowing growth rates.",
    "China alone accounts for over 25% of global emissions (~12.5 Bt), more than double the United States (~5 Bt); India (~3 Bt) is rising fast.",
    "The geographic center of emissions has shifted dramatically: from >90% in Europe and the US in 1900 to Asia producing ~50% today.",
    "Per capita inequalities are extreme \u2014 a 150\u00d7 gap separates the highest emitters (US, Australia at ~15 t) from the lowest (Chad, Niger at ~0.1 t).",
    "Energy mix and policy choices matter: countries with similar prosperity (e.g., France vs. Germany) can have very different per capita emissions.",
]

for i, t in enumerate(takeaways):
    y = Inches(1.5) + Inches(i * 1.1)
    num_shape = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL,
                                    Inches(0.8), y, Inches(0.45), Inches(0.45))
    num_shape.fill.solid()
    num_shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_TEAL
    num_shape.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(s, Inches(0.85), y + Inches(0.03), Inches(0.4), Inches(0.4),
                str(i + 1), font_size=16, bold=True, color=WHITE, alignment=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    add_textbox(s, Inches(1.5), y, Inches(11.0), Inches(0.9),
                t, font_size=16, color=WHITE, line_spacing=1.3)

prs.save(OUT)
print(f"Saved to {OUT}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Global CO₂ Emissions 9-slide deck."""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
import os

ASSETS = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUT = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# Colors
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x2A, 0x4A)
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x00, 0x7B, 0xBB)
ACCENT_TEAL = RGBColor(0x00, 0xA6, 0x9C)
LIGHT_BG = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xF7, 0xFA)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
DARK_TEXT = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x2A, 0x4A)
GRAY_TEXT = RGBColor(0x5A, 0x6A, 0x7A)
RED_ACCENT = RGBColor(0xE0, 0x4F, 0x4F)
GREEN_ACCENT = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x8B, 0x57)
ORANGE_ACCENT = RGBColor(0xE8, 0x8D, 0x2A)
BAR_COLORS = [
    RGBColor(0xC0, 0x39, 0x2B),  # US - red
    RGBColor(0xE8, 0x6D, 0x2A),  # Canada - orange
    RGBColor(0xE8, 0xB8, 0x2A),  # China - gold
    RGBColor(0x2E, 0x86, 0xAB),  # EU-27 - blue
    RGBColor(0x5A, 0x6A, 0x7A),  # World avg - gray
    RGBColor(0x00, 0x7B, 0xBB),  # UK - accent blue
    RGBColor(0x2E, 0x8B, 0x57),  # India - green
    RGBColor(0x8B, 0x6F, 0x4E),  # Chad/Kenya - brown
]

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

SW = prs.slide_width
SH = prs.slide_height

def add_blank_slide():
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    return prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

def add_bg(slide, color):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=DARK_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.2):
